sentences.zh: :《楚辭》者，屈原之所作也。

translations.literal: The Songs of Chu—this was composed by Qu Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Songs of Chu was composed by Qu Yuan.

sentences.zh: 自周室衰亂，詩人寢息，謅佞之道興，諷刺之辭廢。

translations.literal: From the time the Zhou house fell into disorder and decline, poets fell silent; the way of flattery and sycophancy arose, and words of satire and censure were abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou dynasty fell into disorder, the poets fell silent; flattery came into fashion, and satirical remonstrance was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 楚有賢臣屈原，被讒放逐，乃著《離騷》八篇，言己離別愁思，申杼其心，自明無罪，因以諷諫，冀君覺悟，卒不省察，遂赴汨羅死焉。

translations.literal: Chu had the worthy minister Qu Yuan, who, slandered and exiled, then composed eight pieces of "Encountering Sorrow," speaking of his own parting and sorrowful longing, giving voice to his heart, declaring his innocence, and thereby offering satirical remonstrance, hoping the ruler would awaken—yet in the end he was not heeded, and so he went to the Miluo and died there.
translations.idiomatic: Chu had the worthy minister Qu Yuan. Slandered and cast into exile, he composed eight "Encountering Sorrow" poems to voice his grief at parting, lay bare his heart, and proclaim his innocence—offering satirical remonstrance in the hope that his lord might wake to truth. The king never took heed; Qu Yuan drowned himself in the Miluo.

sentences.zh: 弟子宋玉，痛惜其師，傷而和之。

translations.literal: His disciple Song Yu, grieving for his teacher, mourned and responded in kind.
translations.idiomatic: His disciple Song Yu, grieving for his teacher, composed sympathetic pieces in response.

sentences.zh: 其後，賈誼、東方朔、劉向、揚雄，嘉其文彩，擬之而作。

translations.literal: Thereafter Jia Yi, Dongfang Shuo, Liu Xiang, and Yang Xiong, admiring its literary brilliance, modeled themselves on it and composed in that vein.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Jia Yi, Dongfang Shuo, Liu Xiang, and Yang Xiong, admiring its literary brilliance, took it as a model and wrote in the same mode.

sentences.zh: 蓋以原楚人也，謂之「楚辭」。

translations.literal: It was because Yuan was a man of Chu that it was called "Chu Ci."
translations.idiomatic: Because Qu Yuan was a man of Chu, the genre was called the "Songs of Chu."

sentences.zh: 然其氣質高麗，雅致清遠，後之文人，咸不能逮。

translations.literal: Yet its spirit and tone are lofty and splendid, its elegance refined and far-reaching; literati of later ages—none could match it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet its spirit is lofty and resplendent, its elegance refined and far-reaching; no writer of later ages has been able to equal it.

sentences.zh: 始漢武帝命淮南王為之章句，旦受詔，食時而奏之，其書今亡。

translations.literal: At first Emperor Wu of Han ordered the King of Huainan to compose section-and-clause commentary for it; at dawn he received the edict, and by breakfast time he presented it—that book is now lost.
translations.idiomatic: At first Emperor Wu of Han ordered the King of Huainan to compose a section-and-clause commentary on it; the king received the edict at dawn and presented his work by breakfast time—that book is no longer extant.

sentences.zh: 後漢校書郎王逸，集屈原已下，迄于劉向，逸又自為一篇，並敘而注之，今行於世。

translations.literal: Wang Yi, Collator of the Masters of Writing in Later Han, collected [works] from Qu Yuan down through Liu Xiang; Yi also composed one piece himself, and together with a preface annotated them—the edition now current in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi, Collator of the Masters of Writing in Later Han, collected works from Qu Yuan down through Liu Xiang, added one piece of his own, and annotated the whole with a preface—the edition that circulates in the world today.

sentences.zh: 隋時有釋道騫，善讀之，能為楚聲，音韻清切，至今傳《楚辭》者，皆祖騫公之音。

translations.literal: In Sui there was the monk Daojian, skilled at reading it, able to perform in the Chu mode; his tones were clear and sharp—to this day all who transmit The Songs of Chu trace back to Master Qian's pronunciation.
translations.idiomatic: In the Sui dynasty there was the monk Daojian, who read it with great skill and could perform in the Chu mode; his tones were clear and piercing. All who transmit The Songs of Chu today trace their pronunciation back to Master Qian.

sentences.zh: :別集之名，蓋漢東京之所創也。

translations.literal: : The name Separate Collections was probably created in the Eastern Capital of Han.
translations.idiomatic: The category Separate Collections was probably first established in the Eastern Han capital.

sentences.zh: 自靈均已降，屬文之士眾矣，然其志尚不同，風流殊別。

translations.literal: From Qu Yuan onward, writers have been many, yet their aspirations differ and their literary styles are distinct.
translations.idiomatic: From Qu Yuan onward, writers have been numerous, yet their aspirations differ and their literary styles are distinct.

sentences.zh: 後之君子，欲觀其體勢，而見其心靈，故別聚焉，名之為集。

translations.literal: Later gentlemen, wishing to observe their literary forms and see their inner spirit, therefore gathered them separately and called them collections.
translations.idiomatic: Later readers, wishing to observe their literary forms and discern their inner spirit, gathered them separately and called them collections.

sentences.zh: 辭人景慕，並自記載，以成書部。

translations.literal: Writers admired one another and each recorded their own works, thereby forming bibliographic sections.
translations.idiomatic: Writers admired one another and each recorded their own works, thereby forming bibliographic sections.

sentences.zh: 年代遷徙，亦頗遺散。

translations.literal: As ages passed, many were also lost and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: As ages passed, many were also lost and scattered.

sentences.zh: 其高唱絕俗者，略皆具存，今依其先後，次之於此。

translations.literal: Those of elevated voice transcending the common are largely all preserved; they are now arranged here according to chronological order.
translations.idiomatic: Those of elevated voice transcending the common are largely all preserved; they are now arranged here in chronological order.

translations.literal: Boyang Annals, 1 scroll, composed by Xin Yongzhi, Magistrate of Lingling in Song.
translations.idiomatic: Boyang Annals, 1 scroll, composed by Xin Yongzhi, Magistrate of Lingling in Song.

sentences.zh: 亡。

translations.literal: Lost.
translations.idiomatic: Lost.

sentences.zh: 《法集》百七卷梁沙門釋寶唱撰。

translations.literal: Collection of Buddhist Writings, 107 scrolls, composed by the Liang monk Baochang.
translations.idiomatic: Collection of Buddhist Writings, 107 scrolls, composed by the Liang monk Baochang.

sentences.zh: 右一百七部，二千二百一十三卷。

translations.literal: Above: 107 titles, 2,213 scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Above: 107 titles, in 2,213 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 通計亡書，合二百四十九部，五千二百二十四卷。

translations.literal: Counting lost books in total: 249 titles, 5,224 scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Counting lost works as well, 249 titles in 5,224 scrolls in all.

sentences.zh: :總集者，以建安之後，辭賦轉繁，眾家之集，日以滋廣，晉代摯虞苦覽者之勞倦，於是採摘孔翠，芟剪繁蕪，自詩賦下，各為條貫，合而編之，謂為《流別》。

translations.literal: : General Collections—after the Jian'an era rhapsodies and fu grew increasingly numerous, and collections by many authors grew daily more extensive. Zhi Yu of the Jin dynasty, taking pity on the weariness of readers, therefore plucked out the finest gems, cut away luxuriant overgrowth, from poetry and fu downward arranged each in categories, compiled them together, and called this Separate Titles.
translations.idiomatic: General Collections: After the Jian'an era, rhapsodies and fu grew increasingly abundant, and collections by many authors expanded day by day. Zhi Yu of the Jin dynasty, weary of the toil this imposed on readers, therefore selected the finest pieces, pruned away redundant material, and from poetry and fu downward arranged each genre in categories, compiling them into a work called Separate Titles.

sentences.zh: 是後文集總鈔，作者繼軌，屬辭之士，以為覃奧，而取則焉。

translations.literal: After this, general anthologies of collected writings followed in succession; authors continued in their tracks, and men who composed literature regarded them as profound sources and took them as models.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter general anthologies of collected writings appeared one after another; authors followed in succession, and literary men treated them as authoritative compendia and drew their standards from them.

sentences.zh: 今次其前後，並解釋評論，總於此篇。

translations.literal: Now I arrange them in chronological order, together with explanatory commentary, and summarize them all in this treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Here I arrange them in chronological order, with explanatory commentary, gathering them all together in this treatise.

sentences.zh: 凡集五百五十四部，六千六百二十二卷。

translations.literal: Collected works in all: 554 titles, 6,622 scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Collected works in all: 554 titles, in 6,622 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 通計亡書，合一千一百四十六部，一萬三千三百九十卷。

translations.literal: Counting lost books in total: 1,146 titles, 13,390 scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Counting lost works as well, 1,146 titles in 13,390 scrolls in all.

sentences.zh: 【結】文者，所以明言也。

translations.literal: 【Conclusion】 Writing is that by which one clarifies words.
translations.idiomatic: 【Conclusion】 Writing is the means by which one gives clear verbal expression.

sentences.zh: 古者登高能賦，山川能祭，師旅能誓，喪紀能誄，作器能銘，則可以為大夫。

translations.literal: In antiquity, one who could compose fu upon climbing high, perform sacrifices to mountains and rivers, deliver oaths for armies on campaign, write dirges for funeral rites, and inscribe vessels when making implements could become a grandee.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, one who could compose fu upon climbing to a height, offer sacrifices to mountains and rivers, deliver oaths on behalf of armies on campaign, write dirges for funeral observances, and inscribe implements when fashioning vessels could qualify as a grandee.

sentences.zh: 言其因物騁辭，情靈無擁者也。

translations.literal: This means that by taking things as occasion to give free rein to words, feeling and spirit are unconfined.
translations.idiomatic: This means that by taking things as their occasion and giving free rein to language, feeling and spirit remain unconfined.

sentences.zh: 唐歌虞詠，商頌周雅，敘事緣情，紛綸相襲，自斯已降，其道彌繁。

translations.literal: The songs of Tang, the odes of Yu, the hymns of Shang, and the ya of Zhou—narrating events and following feeling—succeeded one another in profusion; from this point downward, the Way grew ever more complex.
translations.idiomatic: From the songs of Tang and the odes of Yu through the hymns of Shang and the ya of Zhou, narrative followed feeling in an unbroken succession of forms; from that time onward, the tradition grew ever more elaborate.

sentences.zh: 世有澆淳，時移治亂，文體遷變，邪正或殊。

translations.literal: Generations have their decadence and purity; times shift between order and disorder; literary forms change and migrate; the heterodox and the orthodox may differ.
translations.idiomatic: Ages differ in moral refinement and decline; times shift between order and chaos; literary forms evolve; and the heterodox and the orthodox may diverge.

sentences.zh: 宋玉、屈原，激清風于南楚，嚴、鄒、枚、馬，陳盛藻於西京，平子豔發於東都，王粲獨步於漳滏。

translations.literal: Song Yu and Qu Yuan stirred clear winds in southern Chu; Yan, Zou, Mei, and Ma displayed luxuriant ornament in the Western Capital; Pingzi bloomed brilliantly in the Eastern Capital; Wang Can walked alone at Zhang and Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yu and Qu Yuan stirred clear winds in southern Chu; Yan Jun, Zou Yang, Mei Sheng, and Sima Xiangru displayed luxuriant ornament in the Western Capital; Zhang Heng bloomed brilliantly in the Eastern Capital; and Wang Can stood unrivaled at Zhang and Fu.

sentences.zh: 愛逮晉氏，見稱潘、陸，並黼藻相輝，宮商間起，清辭潤乎金石，精義薄乎雲天。

translations.literal: Extending to the Jin house, Pan and Lu were praised; both embroidered ornament shone together, musical modes rose in alternation, clear phrasing moistened metal and stone, and refined meaning reached to cloud and sky.
translations.idiomatic: By the Jin dynasty, Pan Yue and Lu Ji were celebrated: their embroidered diction shone in mutual brilliance, tonal patterns rose in alternation, lucid phrasing rang like metal and stone, and refined meaning soared to the clouds.

sentences.zh: 永嘉已後，玄風既扇，辭多平淡，文寡風力。

translations.literal: After the Yongjia era, the abstruse current had already been fanned; diction was mostly plain and bland, and writing lacked vital force.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yongjia era, as the abstruse current gained sway, diction grew largely plain and writing lost much of its vital force.

sentences.zh: 降及江東，不勝其弊。

translations.literal: Descending to the lands east of the Yangzi, one could not bear its defects.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the tradition reached the lands east of the Yangzi, its defects had become unbearable.

sentences.zh: 宋、齊之世，下逮梁初，靈運高致之奇，延年錯綜之美，謝玄暉之藻麗，沈休文之富溢，輝煥斌蔚，辭義可觀。

translations.literal: In the ages of Song and Qi, down to the early Liang, Lingyun's lofty reach was marvelous, Yannian's interwoven beauty, Xie Xuanyhui's florid elegance, and Shen Xiowen's overflowing richness—all brilliant, patterned, and luxuriant, with diction and meaning worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: From the Song and Qi dynasties down to the early Liang, Xie Lingyun's lofty reach was marvelous, Yan Yanshi's interwoven beauty exquisite, Xie Tiao's diction florid and elegant, and Shen Yue's style richly abundant—altogether brilliant and luxuriant, with language and meaning well worth reading.

sentences.zh: 梁簡文之在東宮，亦好篇什，清辭巧制，止乎衽席之間，雕琢蔓藻，思極閨闈之內。

translations.literal: When Liang's Emperor Jianwen was in the Eastern Palace, he also loved pieces and compositions; clear phrasing and clever crafting stopped at the mat and couch, carving and trailing ornament, with thought exhausted within the inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jianwen of Liang was crown prince in the Eastern Palace, he too loved literary composition; his lucid phrasing and artful crafting went no further than the mat and couch, carving ornate diction with thought confined wholly to the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 後生好事，遞相放習，朝野紛紛，號為宮體。

translations.literal: Later youths who delighted in such things imitated one another in succession; court and countryside were in commotion, and it was called Palace Style.
translations.idiomatic: Younger men enamored of such writing imitated one another in turn until court and countryside alike were swept up in the fashion, which came to be called Palace Style.

sentences.zh: 流宕不已，訖於喪亡。

translations.literal: It flowed and wandered without cease, continuing until ruin and extinction.
translations.idiomatic: The fashion ran on without restraint until it ended in dynastic collapse.

sentences.zh: 陳氏因之，未能全變。

translations.literal: The Chen house inherited it and could not wholly change.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen dynasty inherited this tradition and could not wholly break with it.

sentences.zh: 其中原則兵亂積年，文章道盡。

translations.literal: In the Central Plains, by contrast, warfare piled up year after year, and the Way of letters was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: In the Central Plains, by contrast, warfare dragged on for years until the literary tradition itself was exhausted.

sentences.zh: 後魏文帝，頗效屬辭，未能變俗，例皆淳古。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Later Wei somewhat imitated literary composition but could not change custom; cases were all plain and ancient.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Later Wei did attempt literary composition but could not alter prevailing taste; his writings remained uniformly plain and archaic.

sentences.zh: 齊宅漳濱，辭人間起，高言累句，紛紜絡繹，清辭雅致，是所未聞。

translations.literal: Qi established its seat on the banks of the Zhang; men of letters arose among them; lofty words and layered lines were tangled and continuous; clear phrasing was elegant and refined—what had never been heard before.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi established its seat on the banks of the Zhang River, men of letters arose in numbers, piling lofty phrases into layered lines in an unbroken profusion of clear, refined diction such as had never been heard before.

sentences.zh: 後周草創，干戈不戢，君臣戮力，專事經營，風流文雅，我則未暇。

translations.literal: Later Zhou was newly founded; weapons of war were not stilled; ruler and ministers joined strength and devoted themselves wholly to building the state—elegant culture and refinement we had no leisure for.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou was newly founded while weapons of war still had not ceased; ruler and ministers strained every effort toward state-building, and had no leisure for elegant letters.

sentences.zh: 其後南平漢沔，東定河朔，訖于有隋，四海一統，采荊南之梓，收會稽之箭竹，辭人才士，總萃京師。

translations.literal: After this the south was pacified to Han and Mian, the east settled to Heshuo; reaching the Sui, the four seas were unified; catalpa was gathered from south of Jing, arrow bamboo collected from Kuaiji; writers and talented scholars all gathered at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the south was pacified as far as the Han and Mian rivers, the east settled through Heshuo, and under the Sui the empire was unified; catalpa wood was gathered from south of the Jing, arrow bamboo from Kuaiji, and men of letters and talent converged on the capital.

sentences.zh: 屬以高祖少文，煬帝多忌，當路執權，逮相擯壓。

translations.literal: Moreover, because Gaozu cared little for letters and Emperor Yang was much given to suspicion, those in power who held authority successively suppressed and pressed down.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because Emperor Gaozu cared little for literature and Emperor Yang was deeply suspicious, those in power repeatedly suppressed and marginalized literary men.

sentences.zh: 於是握靈蛇之珠，韞荊山之玉，轉死溝壑之內者，不可勝數，草澤怨刺，於是興焉。

translations.literal: Thus those who held pearls of the spirit serpent and concealed jade of Mount Jing, dying turn after turn in ditches and gullies, were beyond counting; resentful satire from the wilds and marshes arose at this.
translations.idiomatic: Thus men who possessed pearls of the spirit serpent and jade of Mount Jing perished by the countless thousands in ditches and gullies, and resentful satire from the wilds and marshes arose in response.

sentences.zh: 古者陳詩觀風，斯亦所以關乎盛衰者也。

translations.literal: In antiquity poems were presented to observe customs—this too is what bears upon rise and decline.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity poems were presented to observe the temper of the age; this too bears directly upon the rise and decline of states.

sentences.zh: 班固有《詩賦略》，凡五種，今引而伸之，合為三種，謂之集部。

translations.literal: Ban Gu had Outline of Poetry and Fu, five kinds in all; now I extend and expand it, combining them into three kinds, called the Collections section.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu's Outline of Poetry and Fu comprised five categories; here I extend and reorganize them into three, called the Collections section.

sentences.zh: 凡四部經傳三千一百二十七部，三萬六千七百八卷。

translations.literal: The four sections of classics and transmissions in all: 3,127 titles, 36,708 scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: The four sections of classics and transmissions comprise 3,127 titles in 36,708 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 通計亡書，合四千一百九十一部，四萬九千四百六十七卷。

translations.literal: Counting lost books in total: 4,191 titles, 49,467 scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Counting lost works as well, 4,191 titles in 49,467 scrolls in all.

sentences.zh: 經戒三百一部，九百八卷。

translations.literal: Scriptural precepts: 301 titles, 908 scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Scriptural precepts: 301 titles, 908 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 餌服四十六部，一百六十七卷。

translations.literal: Ingestible preparations: 46 titles, 167 scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Ingestible preparations: 46 titles, 167 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 房中十三部，三十八卷。

translations.literal: Bedchamber arts: 13 titles, 38 scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Bedchamber arts: 13 titles, 38 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 符錄十七部，一百三卷。

translations.literal: Talismans and registers: 17 titles, 103 scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Talismans and registers: 17 titles, 103 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 右三百七十七部，一千二百一十六卷。

translations.literal: Above: 377 titles, 1,216 scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Above: 377 titles, in 1,216 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 道經道經者，雲有元始天尊，生於太元之先，稟自然之氣，沖虛凝遠，莫知其極。

translations.literal: Daoist scriptures—Daoist scriptures say there is the Primeval Lord of the Way, born before the Grand Origin, endowed with natural qi, empty and still, distant and concentrated, with none knowing his limit.
translations.idiomatic: Daoist Scriptures: Daoist scriptures speak of the Primeval Lord of the Way, born before the Grand Origin, endowed with natural qi—empty, still, and unfathomably remote.

sentences.zh: 所以說天地淪壞，劫數終盡，略與佛經同。

translations.literal: Therefore they speak of heaven and earth collapsing and kalpa numbers ending— broadly the same as Buddhist scriptures.
translations.idiomatic: They teach that heaven and earth collapse and kalpa cycles reach their end—broadly the same doctrine as in Buddhist scriptures.

sentences.zh: 以為天尊之體，常存不滅。

translations.literal: They hold that the body of the Celestial Worthy ever exists and is never extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: They hold that the Celestial Worthy's essence exists eternally and is never destroyed.

sentences.zh: 每至天地初開，或在玉京之上，或在窮桑之野，授以秘道，謂之開劫度人。

translations.literal: Whenever heaven and earth are first opened, whether upon the Jade Capital or in the wilds of Qiong-sang, he bestows the secret Way—this is called opening the kalpa to deliver people.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever heaven and earth are newly opened, whether atop the Jade Capital or in the wilds of Qiongsang, he bestows the secret Way in what is called opening the kalpa to deliver humanity.

sentences.zh: 然其開劫非一度矣，故有延康、赤明、龍漢、開皇，是其年號。

translations.literal: Yet the opening of kalpas is not a single occasion; therefore there are Yankang, Chiming, Longhan, and Kaihuang—these are its era names.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the opening of kalpas has occurred more than once; hence the era names Yankang, Chiming, Longhan, and Kaihuang.

sentences.zh: 其間相去經四十一億萬載。

translations.literal: The intervals between them span four billion myriad ages.
translations.idiomatic: The intervals between them span four billion myriad ages.

sentences.zh: 所度皆諸天仙上品，有太上老君、太上丈人、天真皇人五方天帝及諸仙官，轉共承受，世人莫之豫也。

translations.literal: Those delivered are all highest-grade celestial immortals; there are the Supreme Old Lord, the Supreme Elder, the True Celestial Sovereign, the Five Directional Celestial Emperors, and various immortal officials—turning and jointly receiving in succession; ordinary people do not participate.
translations.idiomatic: Those delivered are all highest-grade celestial immortals—the Supreme Old Lord, the Supreme Elder, the True Celestial Sovereign, the Five Directional Celestial Emperors, and various immortal officials—who receive the teaching in succession; ordinary people have no part in it.

sentences.zh: 所說之經，亦稟元一之氣，自然而有，非所造為，亦與天尊常在不滅。

translations.literal: The scriptures spoken likewise receive the qi of the Primordial One, existing naturally of themselves, not made by creation, and like the Celestial Worthy are ever present and never extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: The scriptures preached likewise arise from the qi of the Primordial One, existing naturally rather than by human creation, and like the Celestial Worthy are eternal and indestructible.

sentences.zh: 天地不壞，則蘊而莫傳，劫運若開，其文自見。

translations.literal: If heaven and earth are not destroyed, they are stored away and not transmitted; if a kalpa cycle opens, their text appears of itself.
translations.idiomatic: While heaven and earth remain intact, the texts lie hidden and untransmitted; when a kalpa cycle opens, their writing appears of itself.

sentences.zh: 凡八字，盡道體之奧，謂之天書。

translations.literal: In all, eight characters exhaust the mystery of the Dao-body—this is called Celestial Script.
translations.idiomatic: Eight characters in all exhaust the mystery of the Dao-body; this is called Celestial Script.

sentences.zh: 字方一丈，八角垂芒，光輝照耀，驚心眩目，雖諸天仙，不能省視。

translations.literal: Each character is one zhang square, with eight corners and hanging rays; brilliance shines and dazzles, startling the heart and blinding the eyes—even celestial immortals cannot examine and view them.
translations.idiomatic: Each character measures one zhang square, with eight corners and radiating rays; their brilliance dazzles the eyes and staggers the heart—even celestial immortals cannot gaze upon them directly.

sentences.zh: 天尊之開劫也，乃命天真皇人，改囀天音而辯析之。

translations.literal: When the Celestial Worthy opens a kalpa, he then commands the True Celestial Sovereign to convert and recite the celestial sounds and analyze them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Celestial Worthy opens a kalpa, he commands the True Celestial Sovereign to translate the celestial sounds and expound their meaning.

sentences.zh: 自天真以下，至於諸仙，輾轉節級，以次相授。

translations.literal: From the True Celestial Sovereign downward to the various immortals, turning and passing through graded ranks, they transmit in sequence one to another.
translations.idiomatic: From the True Celestial Sovereign down through the ranks of immortals, the teaching passes in graded succession from one to the next.

sentences.zh: 諸仙得之，始授世人。

translations.literal: When the immortals obtain it, they then transmit it to people of the world.
translations.idiomatic: Only when the immortals receive it do they transmit it to people of the world.

sentences.zh: 然以天尊經歷年載，始一開劫，受法之人，得而寶秘，亦有年限，方始傳授。

translations.literal: Yet because the Celestial Worthy passes through years and ages before opening a kalpa once, those who receive the Law obtain it and treasure it in secrecy; there are also term limits before transmission begins.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because ages pass before the Celestial Worthy opens a kalpa, those who receive the Law hold it as a treasured secret and may transmit it only after a prescribed term.

sentences.zh: 上品則年久，下品則年近。

translations.literal: Higher grades then have longer years; lower grades have years nearer.
translations.idiomatic: Higher grades require longer terms; lower grades shorter ones.

sentences.zh: 故今授道者，經四十九年，始得授人。

translations.literal: Therefore those who now transmit the Way, after forty-nine years, may begin to transmit to others.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore one who transmits the Way today must wait forty-nine years before teaching another.

sentences.zh: 推其大旨，蓋亦歸於仁愛清靜，積而修習，漸致長生，自然神化，或白日登仙，與道合體。

translations.literal: Inferring its great purport, it broadly also returns to benevolence, love, clarity, and stillness; accumulating and cultivating practice, one gradually attains long life, natural divine transformation, or ascending as immortal in broad daylight, merging body with the Way.
translations.idiomatic: In its broad purport, the teaching returns to benevolence, clarity, and stillness; through accumulated practice one gradually attains long life and divine transformation, ascending as an immortal in broad daylight and merging with the Way.

sentences.zh: 其受道之法，初受《五千文籙》，次受《三洞籙》，次受《洞玄籙》，次受《上清籙》。

translations.literal: The method of receiving the Way: first receive the Register of the Five Thousand Characters; next receive the Register of the Three Caverns; next receive the Register of Cavern Mystery; next receive the Register of Upper Clarity.
translations.idiomatic: The method of receiving the Way proceeds in stages: first the Register of the Five Thousand Characters, then the Register of the Three Caverns, then the Register of Cavern Mystery, and finally the Register of Upper Clarity.

sentences.zh: 籙皆素書，紀諸天曹官屬佐吏之名有多少，又有諸符，錯在其間，文章詭怪，世所不識。

translations.literal: Registers are all plain writing, recording the names of officials, attendants, and clerks of the various celestial bureaus in their numbers; there are also various talismans interspersed among them—the writing strange and uncanny, unrecognized by the world.
translations.idiomatic: The registers are written on plain silk, listing the names and ranks of officials and clerks in the celestial bureaus, with various talismans interspersed—writing so strange that the world cannot decipher it.

sentences.zh: 受者必先潔齋，然後齎金環一，並諸贄幣，以見於師。

translations.literal: The recipient must first perform purification fasting, then carry one gold ring together with various tribute gifts to appear before the master.
translations.idiomatic: The recipient must first undergo purification fasting, then present one gold ring together with the prescribed tribute gifts before the master.

sentences.zh: 師受其贄，以籙授之，仍剖金環，各持其半，雲以為約。

translations.literal: The master receives the tribute and bestows the register; then the gold ring is split, each holding half—they say this serves as covenant.
translations.idiomatic: The master accepts the tribute and bestows the register, then splits the gold ring so each party keeps half as a covenant.

sentences.zh: 弟子得籙，緘而佩之。

translations.literal: When the disciple obtains the register, he seals it and wears it.
translations.idiomatic: The disciple seals the register upon receiving it and wears it on the person.

sentences.zh: 其潔齋之法，有黃籙、玉籙、金籙、塗炭等齋。

translations.literal: The methods of purification fasting include Yellow Register, Jade Register, Gold Register, and Smearing with Ash fasts, among others.
translations.idiomatic: Methods of purification fasting include the Yellow Register, Jade Register, Gold Register, and Smearing-with-Ash fasts, among others.

sentences.zh: 為壇三成，每成皆置綿蕝嶠，以為限域。

translations.literal: An altar is made in three tiers; on each tier cotton curtains and barriers are set as delimited bounds.
translations.idiomatic: An altar is built in three tiers, each enclosed with cotton curtains and barriers to mark the sacred precinct.

sentences.zh: 傍各開門，皆有法象。

translations.literal: On the sides gates are opened at each point; all have ritual emblems.
translations.idiomatic: Gates are opened on each side, each bearing its prescribed ritual emblems.

sentences.zh: 齋者亦有人數之限，以次入於綿蕝之中，魚貫面縛，陳說愆咎，告白神祇，晝夜不息，或一二七日而止。

translations.literal: Those fasting also have limits on numbers; entering the cotton enclosure in sequence, they file in single file with faces bound, stating faults and offenses, declaring them to the spirits, day and night without cease, stopping after one or two or seven days.
translations.idiomatic: The number of participants is also limited; they enter the curtained enclosure in single file with faces bound, confessing faults and offenses to the spirits day and night without cease for one, two, or seven days.

sentences.zh: 其齋數之外有人者，並在綿蕝之外，謂之齋客，但拜謝而已，不面縛焉。

translations.literal: Those beyond the limit of fasting participants all remain outside the cotton enclosure—they are called fasting guests and only bow in thanks; they are not face-bound.
translations.idiomatic: Those beyond the prescribed number remain outside the enclosure as fasting guests, offering bows of thanks but not binding their faces.

sentences.zh: 而又有諸消災度厄之法，依陰陽五行數術，推人年命書之，如章表之儀，並具贄幣，燒香陳讀。

translations.literal: There are also various methods of dispelling disaster and crossing calamity; relying on yin-yang, the five phases, and numerological arts, one calculates a person's year and fate and writes it in the form of memorials and petitions, together preparing tribute gifts, burning incense and reciting aloud.
translations.idiomatic: There are also methods for dispelling disaster and averting calamity, which calculate a person's fate by yin-yang and the five phases, compose petitions in the form of official memorials, prepare tribute gifts, burn incense, and recite them aloud.

sentences.zh: 雲奏上天曹，請為除厄，謂之上章。

translations.literal: They say it is submitted to the celestial bureau above, requesting removal of calamity—this is called submitting a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: It is said to be submitted to the celestial bureau above with a request to remove calamity; this is called submitting a memorial.

sentences.zh: 夜中於星辰之下，陳設酒脯餅餌幣物，曆祀天皇太一，祀五星列宿，為書如上章之儀以奏之，名之為醮。

translations.literal: In the middle of the night beneath the stars, wine, dried meats, cakes, offerings, and tribute goods are set out; sequentially sacrificing to the Celestial Emperor and Grand Unity, sacrificing to the five stars and lunar lodges, composing writing in the ritual of submitting memorials to present it—this is named a jiao offering.
translations.idiomatic: In the depths of night beneath the stars, wine, dried meats, cakes, and tribute offerings are set out; the Celestial Emperor, Grand Unity, the five stars, and the lunar lodges are worshipped in succession, and a petition composed in the same form as a memorial is presented—this is called a jiao offering.

sentences.zh: 又以木為印，刻星辰日月於其上，吸氣執之，以印疾病，多有愈者。

translations.literal: Also a seal is made of wood, with stars, sun, and moon carved upon it; inhaling qi and holding it, one stamps it upon illness—many are healed.
translations.idiomatic: They also carve stars, sun, and moon on a wooden seal, inhale qi while holding it, and stamp it upon the afflicted—many recover thereby.

sentences.zh: 又能登刀入火而焚敕之，使刃不能割，火不能熱。

translations.literal: They can also tread upon blades and enter fire while burning talismanic commands, so blades cannot cut and fire cannot burn.
translations.idiomatic: They can also tread on blades and walk through fire while burning talismanic commands, so that blades cannot cut them nor fire burn them.

sentences.zh: 而又有諸服餌、辟谷、金丹、玉漿、雲英，蠲除滓穢之法，不可殫記。

translations.literal: There are also various methods of ingesting medicines, grain avoidance, golden elixirs, jade broth, and cloud essences for removing impurities—impossible to record exhaustively.
translations.idiomatic: There are also innumerable methods of ingesting medicines, abstaining from grain, refining golden elixirs and jade broth, and purging impurities—too many to record in full.

sentences.zh: 雲自上古黃帝、帝嚳、夏禹之儔，並遇神人，咸受道籙，年代既遠，經史無聞焉。

translations.literal: They say that from high antiquity the Yellow Emperor, Emperor Ku, Yu of Xia, and their kind all encountered divine persons and alike received Dao registers—but the ages are already distant, and the classics and histories have no report of this.
translations.idiomatic: They claim that from high antiquity the Yellow Emperor, Emperor Ku, Yu of Xia, and their like all encountered divine beings and received Daoist registers—but the ages are remote and the classics and histories say nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 推尋事蹟，漢時諸子，道書之流有三十七家，大旨皆去健羨，處沖虛而已，無上天官符籙之事。

translations.literal: Tracing affairs and traces, among Han masters the stream of Daoist books had thirty-seven schools; their great purport was all to remove vigor and envy and abide in empty stillness—there were no matters of celestial officials, talismans, and registers.
translations.idiomatic: Tracing the historical record, the Daoist books of Han masters numbered thirty-seven schools, all broadly teaching detachment from ambition and abiding in empty stillness—nothing of celestial officials, talismans, or registers.

sentences.zh: 其《黃帝》四篇，《老子》二篇，最得深旨。

translations.literal: Among them, the four chapters of the Yellow Emperor and the two chapters of the Old Master most attained the deep purport.
translations.idiomatic: Of these, the four chapters of the Yellow Emperor and the two chapters of Laozi best capture the deep purport.

sentences.zh: 故言陶弘景者，隱于句容，好陰陽五行，風角星算，修辟穀導引之法，受道經符籙，武帝素與之遊。

translations.literal: Thus concerning Tao Hongjing: he retired to Jurong, loved yin-yang and the five phases, wind divination and star calculation, cultivated grain avoidance and daoyin methods, received Daoist scriptures, talismans, and registers; Emperor Wu had long associated with him.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Hongjing, for example, retired to Jurong, devoted himself to yin-yang, the five phases, wind divination, and star calculation, practiced grain avoidance and daoyin exercises, and received Daoist scriptures, talismans, and registers; Emperor Wu of Liang had long been his companion.

sentences.zh: 及禪代之際，弘景取圖讖之文，合成「景梁」字以獻之，由是恩遇甚厚。

translations.literal: At the time of the abdication and succession, Hongjing took prognostic texts and combined characters to form "Jing Liang" to present them; by this his favor and treatment were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: At the abdication, Hongjing drew on prognostic texts to compose the characters "Jing Liang" and presented them to the throne, winning extraordinary favor thereby.

sentences.zh: 又撰《登真隱訣》，以證古有神仙之事；

translations.literal: He also composed Secret Instructions on Ascending to Truth to verify that antiquity had matters of immortals;
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Secret Instructions on Ascending to Truth to demonstrate that immortals existed in antiquity;

sentences.zh: 又言神丹可成，服之則能長生，與天地永畢。

translations.literal: he also said divine elixirs could be achieved; ingesting them one could attain long life and end together with heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: and claimed that divine elixirs could be perfected, and that ingesting them would grant long life coextensive with heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 帝令弘景試合神丹，竟不能就，乃言中原隔絕，藥物不精故也。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Hongjing to attempt compounding divine elixir; in the end he could not succeed, and then said the Central Plains were cut off and medicines were not refined—this was the reason.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Hongjing to attempt compounding a divine elixir; when he failed, he explained that the Central Plains were cut off and medicinal ingredients were not pure enough.

sentences.zh: 帝以為然，敬之尤甚。

translations.literal: The emperor considered this so and revered him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this explanation and revered him all the more.

sentences.zh: 然武帝弱年好事，先受道法，及即位，猶自上章，朝士受道者眾。

translations.literal: Yet Emperor Wu in his youth delighted in such things, first receiving Daoist methods; upon acceding to the throne, he still submitted memorials himself, and many court officials received the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu had been devoted to such pursuits from youth and received Daoist teaching early; even after acceding to the throne he continued submitting memorials to heaven, and many court officials received the Way.

sentences.zh: 三吳及邊海之際，信之逾甚。

translations.literal: In the Three Wu regions and along the coastal borders, belief was even more intense.
translations.idiomatic: In the Three Wu region and along the coast, belief ran even deeper.

sentences.zh: 陳武世居吳興，故亦奉焉。

translations.literal: Chen Wu for generations resided in Wuxing, and therefore also honored it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Chen came from Wuxing by descent and likewise honored the faith.

sentences.zh: 後魏之世，嵩山道士寇謙之，自雲嘗遇真人成公興，後遇太上老君，授謙之為天師，而又賜之《雲中音誦科誡》二十卷。

translations.literal: In the age of Later Wei, the Mount Song Daoist Kou Qizhi said he once encountered the perfected Cheng Gongxing, and later encountered the Supreme Old Lord, who appointed Qizhi as Celestial Master and moreover bestowed upon him twenty scrolls of Precepts for Chanting in the Clouds.
translations.idiomatic: In Later Wei, the Mount Song Daoist Kou Qizhi claimed to have encountered the perfected Cheng Gongxing and later the Supreme Old Lord, who appointed him Celestial Master and bestowed twenty scrolls of Precepts for Chanting in the Clouds.

sentences.zh: 又使玉女授其服氣導引之法，遂得辟谷，氣盛體輕，顏色鮮麗。

translations.literal: A jade maiden also taught him methods of ingesting qi and daoyin; he then attained grain avoidance, with qi abundant and body light, complexion fresh and bright.
translations.idiomatic: A jade maiden also taught him methods of ingesting qi and daoyin; he attained grain avoidance, his qi flourished and his body grew light, and his complexion brightened.

sentences.zh: 弟子十余人，皆得其術。

translations.literal: More than ten disciples all obtained his methods.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten disciples all mastered his methods.

sentences.zh: 其後又遇神人李譜，雲是老君玄孫，授其圖籙真經，劾召百神，六十餘卷，及銷煉金丹雲英八石玉漿之法。

translations.literal: Afterward he again encountered the divine person Li Pu, who said he was the mysterious grandson of the Old Lord, bestowing upon him chart registers and true scriptures for commanding and summoning the hundred spirits, more than sixty scrolls, and methods for refining golden elixirs, cloud essences, eight-stone preparations, and jade broth.
translations.idiomatic: He later encountered the divine being Li Pu, who claimed to be the Old Lord's distant descendant, and received from him chart registers and true scriptures for summoning the hundred spirits in more than sixty scrolls, together with methods for refining golden elixirs, cloud essences, eight-stone preparations, and jade broth.

sentences.zh: 太武始光之初，奉其書而獻之。

translations.literal: In the beginning of the Shiguang era of Emperor Taiwu, he presented and offered his books.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Shiguang era under Emperor Taiwu of Northern Wei, he presented these writings to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝使謁者，奉玉帛牲牢，祀嵩嶽，迎致其餘弟子，于代都東南起壇宇，給道士百二十余人，顯揚其法，宣佈天下。

translations.literal: The emperor sent an usher bearing jade silks and sacrificial victims to sacrifice at Mount Song, welcoming and bringing his remaining disciples; southeast of the capital at Dai he raised altar halls, supplying more than 120 Daoists, displaying and spreading his Law, proclaiming it throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an envoy with jade silks and sacrificial victims to worship at Mount Song, summoned Qizhi's remaining disciples, built altar halls southeast of the capital at Dai, supported more than 120 Daoists, and proclaimed the teaching throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 太武親備法駕而受符籙焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu personally prepared the ritual carriage and received talismans and registers.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu personally rode in the imperial ritual carriage to receive talismans and registers.

sentences.zh: 自是道業大行，每帝即位，必受符籙，以為故事，刻天尊及諸仙之象而供養焉。

translations.literal: From this the Daoist enterprise greatly flourished; each emperor upon accession necessarily received talismans and registers as established precedent, carving images of the Celestial Worthy and various immortals to venerate them.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Daoism flourished widely; each new emperor received talismans and registers upon accession as established precedent, and images of the Celestial Worthy and various immortals were carved for veneration.

sentences.zh: 遷洛已後，置道場於南郊之傍，方二百步。

translations.literal: After the move to Luoyang, a ritual precinct was established beside the southern suburb, two hundred paces square.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital moved to Luoyang, a ritual precinct two hundred paces square was established beside the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 正月、十月之十五日，並有道士哥人百六人，拜而祠焉。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth days of the first and tenth months, there were always 106 Daoists chanting, bowing and sacrificing there.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth day of the first and tenth months, 106 Daoists would chant and perform sacrifices there.

sentences.zh: 後齊神武帝遷鄴，遂罷之。

translations.literal: Later, when Emperor Shenwu of Qi moved to Ye, it was then abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenwu of Northern Qi moved the capital to Ye, the practice was abolished.

sentences.zh: 文襄之世，更置館宇，選其精至者使居焉。

translations.literal: In the age of Wenxiang, halls were again established, selecting the most refined to dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wenxiang, halls were re-established and the most accomplished practitioners were selected to reside there.

sentences.zh: 後周承魏，崇奉道法，每帝受籙，如魏之舊，尋與佛法俱滅，開皇初又興，高祖雅信佛法，于道士蔑如也。

translations.literal: Later Zhou inherited Wei, honoring and revering the Daoist Law; each emperor received registers as in Wei's old way; soon it perished together with Buddhist Law; at the beginning of Kaihuang it revived again; Gaozu elegantly trusted Buddhist Law and regarded Daoists with disdain.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou inherited Wei and honored the Daoist Law; each emperor received registers as in the Wei tradition, but the practice soon perished together with Buddhism, revived briefly at the opening of Kaihuang, while Emperor Gaozu devoted himself to Buddhism and held Daoists in contempt.

sentences.zh: 大業中，道士以術進者甚眾。

translations.literal: In the Daye era, Daoists who advanced by arts and techniques were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era, many Daoists gained favor at court through their arts.

sentences.zh: 其所以講經，由以《老子》為本，次講《莊子》及《靈寶》、《升玄》之屬。

translations.literal: Their method of expounding scriptures takes the Old Master as foundation, next expounding Zhuangzi and works such as Lingbao and Shengxuan.
translations.idiomatic: In expounding scriptures they take Laozi as the foundation, followed by Zhuangzi and texts of the Lingbao and Shengxuan traditions.

sentences.zh: 其餘眾經，或言傳之神人，篇卷非一。

translations.literal: The remaining various scriptures, some say transmitted by divine persons, have chapters and scrolls not of one kind.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining scriptures, said by some to have been transmitted by divine beings, exist in many volumes.

sentences.zh: 自雲天尊姓樂名靜信，例皆淺俗，故世甚疑之。

translations.literal: They themselves say the Celestial Worthy's surname is Yue and given name Jingxin; cases are all shallow and vulgar, and therefore the world greatly doubts them.
translations.idiomatic: They claim the Celestial Worthy's surname is Yue and given name Jingxin; the writings are uniformly crude and vulgar, and the world regards them with deep suspicion.

sentences.zh: 其術業優者，行諸符禁，往往神驗。

translations.literal: Those superior in arts and practice, performing various talismanic prohibitions, often have divine verification.
translations.idiomatic: Those most skilled in the arts, performing talismanic rites, often produce results that seem miraculous.

sentences.zh: 而金丹玉液長生之事，歷代糜費，不可勝紀，竟無效焉。

translations.literal: Yet matters of golden elixirs, jade broth, and long life—dynasties wasted resources beyond counting, and in the end there was no effect.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the pursuit of golden elixirs, jade broth, and immortality has consumed resources beyond reckoning through the ages, all to no effect.

sentences.zh: 今考其經目之數，附之於此。

translations.literal: Now I examine the numbers of their scripture catalog and append them here.
translations.idiomatic: Here I set out the numbers of their scripture catalog.

sentences.zh: 大乘經六百一十七部，二千七十六卷。

translations.literal: Mahayana scriptures: 617 titles, 2,076 scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Mahayana scriptures: 617 titles, 2,076 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 五百五十八部，一千六百九十七卷，經。

translations.literal: 558 titles, 1,697 scrolls—scriptures.
translations.idiomatic: 558 titles, 1,697 scrolls—scriptures.

sentences.zh: 五十九部，三百七十九卷，疏。

translations.literal: 59 titles, 379 scrolls—commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: 59 titles, 379 scrolls—commentaries.

sentences.zh: 小乘經四百八十七部，八百五十二卷。

translations.literal: Hinayana scriptures: 487 titles, 852 scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Hinayana scriptures: 487 titles, 852 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 雜經三百八十部，七百一十六卷。

translations.literal: Miscellaneous scriptures: 380 titles, 716 scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous scriptures: 380 titles, 716 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 雜經目殘缺，其見數如此。

translations.literal: The catalog of miscellaneous scriptures is incomplete and deficient; the surviving numbers are as follows.
translations.idiomatic: The catalog of miscellaneous scriptures is incomplete; the surviving count is as given above.

sentences.zh: 雜疑經一百七十二部，三百三十六卷。

translations.literal: Miscellaneous doubtful scriptures: 172 titles, 336 scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous doubtful scriptures: 172 titles, 336 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 大乘律五十二部，九十一卷。

translations.literal: Mahayana vinaya: 52 titles, 91 scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Mahayana vinaya: 52 titles, 91 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 小乘律八十部，四百七十二卷。

translations.literal: Hinayana vinaya: 80 titles, 472 scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Hinayana vinaya: 80 titles, 472 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 七十七部，四百九十卷，律。

translations.literal: 77 titles, 490 scrolls—vinaya.
translations.idiomatic: 77 titles, 490 scrolls—vinaya.

sentences.zh: 二部，二十三卷，講疏。

translations.literal: 2 titles, 23 scrolls—lecture commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: 2 titles, 23 scrolls—lecture commentaries.

sentences.zh: 雜律二十七部，四十六卷。

translations.literal: Miscellaneous vinaya: 27 titles, 46 scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous vinaya: 27 titles, 46 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 大乘論三十五部，一百四十一卷。

translations.literal: Mahayana treatises: 35 titles, 141 scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Mahayana treatises: 35 titles, 141 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 三十部，九十四卷，論。

translations.literal: 30 titles, 94 scrolls—treatises.
translations.idiomatic: 30 titles, 94 scrolls—treatises.

sentences.zh: 十五部，四十七卷，疏。

translations.literal: 15 titles, 47 scrolls—commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: 15 titles, 47 scrolls—commentaries.

sentences.zh: 小乘論四十一部，五百六十七卷。

translations.literal: Hinayana treatises: 41 titles, 567 scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Hinayana treatises: 41 titles, 567 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 二十一部，四百九十一卷，論。

translations.literal: 21 titles, 491 scrolls—treatises.
translations.idiomatic: 21 titles, 491 scrolls—treatises.

sentences.zh: 十部，七十六卷，講疏。

translations.literal: 10 titles, 76 scrolls—lecture commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: 10 titles, 76 scrolls—lecture commentaries.

sentences.zh: 雜論五十一部，四百三十七卷。

translations.literal: Miscellaneous treatises: 51 titles, 437 scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous treatises: 51 titles, 437 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 三十二部，二百九十九卷，論。

translations.literal: 32 titles, 299 scrolls—treatises.
translations.idiomatic: 32 titles, 299 scrolls—treatises.

sentences.zh: 九部，一百三十八卷，講疏。

translations.literal: 9 titles, 138 scrolls—lecture commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: 9 titles, 138 scrolls—lecture commentaries.

sentences.zh: 記二十部，四百六十四卷。

translations.literal: Records: 20 titles, 464 scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Records: 20 titles, 464 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 右一千九百五十部，六千一百九十八卷。

translations.literal: At right: 1,950 titles, 6,198 scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: In all: 1,950 titles, 6,198 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 佛經佛經者，西域天竺之迦維衛國淨飯王太子釋迦牟尼所說。

translations.literal: Buddhist scriptures—what are called Buddhist scriptures are those spoken by Śākyamuni, crown prince of King Śuddhodana of Kapilavastu in India of the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhist scriptures are the teachings spoken by Śākyamuni, crown prince of King Śuddhodana of Kapilavastu in India of the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 釋迦當周莊王之九年四月八日，自母右脅而生，姿貌奇異，有三十二相，八十二好。

translations.literal: Śākyamuni, in the ninth year of King Zhuang of Zhou on the eighth day of the fourth month, was born from his mother's right side; his appearance was extraordinary, having thirty-two major marks and eighty minor excellences.
translations.idiomatic: Śākyamuni was born from his mother's right side on the eighth day of the fourth month in the ninth year of King Zhuang of Zhou; his appearance was extraordinary, marked by the thirty-two major signs and eighty minor excellences.

sentences.zh: 舍太子位，出家學道，勤行精進，覺悟一切種智，而謂之佛，亦曰佛陀，亦曰浮屠，皆胡言也。

translations.literal: He relinquished the crown prince's position, left home to study the Way, diligently practiced with ardor, awakened to omniscience, and was therefore called Buddha; also called Fótú or Fútú—all foreign terms.
translations.idiomatic: He renounced the crown prince's station, left home to pursue the Way, practiced diligently with ardor, and awakened to omniscience; he was therefore called Buddha, or Fótú, or Fútú—all foreign terms.

sentences.zh: 華言譯之為淨覺。

translations.literal: In Chinese it is rendered "Pure Awakening."
translations.idiomatic: In Chinese it is rendered "Pure Awakening."

sentences.zh: 其所說雲，人身雖有生死之異，至於精神則恆不滅。

translations.literal: What he taught runs thus: though the human body has differences of birth and death, as for the spirit it is constantly undying.
translations.idiomatic: His teaching holds that though the human body undergoes birth and death, the spirit is eternally undying.

sentences.zh: 此身之前，則經無量身矣。

translations.literal: Before this body, one has already passed through innumerable bodies.
translations.idiomatic: Before this present body, one has already passed through innumerable bodies.

sentences.zh: 積而修習，精神清淨，則成佛道。

translations.literal: Accumulating and cultivating practice, when the spirit is pure and clear, one then attains Buddhahood.
translations.idiomatic: Through accumulated cultivation, when the spirit grows pure and clear, one attains Buddhahood.

sentences.zh: 天地之外，四維上下，更有天地，亦無終極，然皆有成有敗。

translations.literal: Beyond heaven and earth, in the four directions and above and below, there are further heavens and earths without end or limit, yet all have formation and destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond heaven and earth, in every direction above and below, lie further heavens and earths without end, yet all undergo formation and destruction.

sentences.zh: 一成一敗，謂之一劫。

translations.literal: One formation and one destruction is called one kalpa.
translations.idiomatic: One formation and one destruction constitute a kalpa.

sentences.zh: 自此天地已前，則有無量劫矣。

translations.literal: Before this heaven and earth, there have been innumerable kalpas.
translations.idiomatic: Before this heaven and earth came into being, there were innumerable kalpas.

sentences.zh: 每劫必有諸佛得道，出世教化，其數不同。

translations.literal: In each kalpa there are necessarily Buddhas who attain the Way, appear in the world, and teach—their numbers differ.
translations.idiomatic: In each kalpa Buddhas necessarily attain the Way, appear in the world, and teach, though their numbers differ.

sentences.zh: 今此劫中，當有千佛。

translations.literal: In the present kalpa there will be a thousand Buddhas.
translations.idiomatic: In the present kalpa there will be a thousand Buddhas.

sentences.zh: 自初至於釋迦，已七佛矣。

translations.literal: From the first up to Śākyamuni, there have already been seven Buddhas.
translations.idiomatic: From the first up to Śākyamuni, seven Buddhas have already appeared.

sentences.zh: 其次當有彌勒出世，必經三會，演說法藏，開度眾生。

translations.literal: Next Maitreya will appear in the world, must pass through three assemblies, expound the treasury of the Law, and open and deliver living beings.
translations.idiomatic: Next Maitreya will appear in the world, hold three assemblies, expound the treasury of the Law, and deliver living beings.

sentences.zh: 由其道者，有四等之果。

translations.literal: Those who follow this Way obtain fruits of four ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Those who follow this Way attain fruits of four ranks.

sentences.zh: 一曰須陀洹，二曰斯陀含，三曰阿那含，四曰阿羅漢。

translations.literal: The first is srotāpanna, the second sakṛdāgāmin, the third anāgāmin, the fourth arhat.
translations.idiomatic: The first is srotāpanna, the second sakṛdāgāmin, the third anāgāmin, the fourth arhat.

sentences.zh: 至羅漢者，則出入生死，去來隱顯，而不為累。

translations.literal: When one reaches arhatship, one enters and exits birth and death, coming and going, hiding and appearing, yet is not burdened thereby.
translations.idiomatic: When one reaches arhatship, one moves freely through birth and death, appearing and vanishing at will, yet remains unburdened.

sentences.zh: 阿羅漢已上，至菩薩者，深見佛性，以至成道。

translations.literal: Above arhat up to bodhisattva, one deeply perceives buddha-nature, progressing to attainment of the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Above arhatship, bodhisattvas deeply perceive buddha-nature and progress to full enlightenment.

sentences.zh: 每佛滅度，遺法相傳，有正、象、末三等淳樗之異。

translations.literal: When each Buddha enters parinirvāṇa, the Dharma left behind is transmitted in succession, with differences of three grades—correct, semblance, and final—of purity and decay.
translations.idiomatic: When each Buddha enters parinirvāṇa, the Dharma he leaves behind is transmitted in succession, passing through three ages—correct, semblance, and final—of varying purity and decline.

sentences.zh: 年歲遠近，亦各不同。

translations.literal: The length of years, near or far, also differs in each case.
translations.idiomatic: The duration of each age also differs.

sentences.zh: 末法已後，眾生愚鈍，無複佛教，而業行轉惡，年壽漸短，經數百千載間，乃至朝生夕死。

translations.literal: After the final Dharma age, living beings grow dull and obtuse, Buddhism ceases again, karmic conduct turns increasingly evil, lifespans gradually shorten, and within hundreds or thousands of years some are born in the morning and die at evening.
translations.idiomatic: After the final Dharma age, living beings grow dull and obtuse, Buddhism disappears, karmic conduct worsens, lifespans shrink, and within a few hundred or thousand years some live only from morning till evening.

sentences.zh: 然後有大水、大火、大風之災，一切除去之，而更立生人，又歸淳樸，謂之小劫。

translations.literal: Then come disasters of great flood, great fire, and great wind, which remove everything, and new human life is established again, returning to simplicity—this is called a minor kalpa.
translations.idiomatic: Then come disasters of great flood, fire, and wind that sweep everything away; new human life is created and the world returns to simplicity—this is called a minor kalpa.

sentences.zh: 每一小劫，則一佛出世。

translations.literal: In each minor kalpa one Buddha appears in the world.
translations.idiomatic: In each minor kalpa one Buddha appears in the world.

sentences.zh: 初，天竺中多諸外道，並事水火毒龍，而善諸變幻。

translations.literal: At the beginning, in India there were many heterodox paths, all serving water, fire, and venomous dragons, and skilled in various transformations.
translations.idiomatic: In early times India had many heterodox sects, all worshipping water, fire, and venomous dragons and adept at various transformations.

sentences.zh: 釋迦之苦行也，是諸邪道，並來嬲惱，以亂其心，而不能得。

translations.literal: During Śākyamuni's ascetic practices, these heterodox paths all came to harass and torment him, seeking to disturb his mind, yet could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: During Śākyamuni's ascetic practices, these heterodox sects all came to harass and torment him, seeking to unsettle his mind, but could not succeed.

sentences.zh: 及佛道成，盡皆摧伏，並為弟子。

translations.literal: When the Buddha-Way was accomplished, they were all overthrown and subdued and all became disciples.
translations.idiomatic: When the Buddha-Way was accomplished, they were all overthrown and subdued and became his disciples.

sentences.zh: 弟子，男曰桑門，譯言息心，而總曰僧，譯言行乞。

translations.literal: Disciples—men are called śramaṇa, rendered "stilling the mind"; collectively called monks (seng), rendered "mendicants."
translations.idiomatic: Disciples—men are called śramaṇa, rendered "stilling the mind"; collectively they are called monks (seng), rendered "mendicants."

sentences.zh: 女曰比丘尼。

translations.literal: Women are called bhikṣuṇī.
translations.idiomatic: Women are called bhikṣuṇī.

sentences.zh: 皆剃落鬚髮，釋累辭家，相與和居，治心修淨，行乞以自資，而防心攝行。

translations.literal: All shave head and beard, cast off burdens and leave home, dwell together in harmony, cultivate the mind and pursue purity, beg for sustenance, and guard the mind and restrain conduct.
translations.idiomatic: All shave head and beard, cast off worldly burdens and leave home, dwell together in harmony, cultivate the mind and pursue purity, support themselves by begging, and guard the mind while restraining conduct.

sentences.zh: 僧至二百五十戒，尼五百戒。

translations.literal: Monks have up to 250 precepts; nuns 500.
translations.idiomatic: Monks observe up to 250 precepts; nuns 500.

sentences.zh: 俗人信憑佛法者，男曰優婆塞，女曰優婆夷，皆去殺、盜、淫、妄言、飲酒，是為五誡。

translations.literal: Lay devotees who rely on the Buddhist Law—men are called upāsaka, women upāsikā; all refrain from killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, false speech, and drinking wine—these are the five precepts.
translations.idiomatic: Lay devotees who rely on the Buddhist Law—men are called upāsaka, women upāsikā; all refrain from killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, false speech, and drinking wine—these are the five precepts.

sentences.zh: 釋迦在世教化四十九年，乃至天龍人鬼並來聽法，弟子得道，以百千萬億數。

translations.literal: Śākyamuni, while in the world, taught for forty-nine years; even dragons, humans, and ghosts all came to hear the Law; disciples who attained the Way numbered in the hundreds of thousands of myriads of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Śākyamuni taught in the world for forty-nine years; dragons, humans, and ghosts all came to hear the Law, and disciples who attained the Way numbered in the hundreds of thousands of myriads of millions.

sentences.zh: 然後於拘屍那城娑羅雙樹間，以二月十五日，入般涅槃。

translations.literal: Then at Kuśinagara between the twin śāla trees, on the fifteenth day of the second month, he entered parinirvāṇa.
translations.idiomatic: Then at Kuśinagara between the twin śāla trees, on the fifteenth day of the second month, he entered parinirvāṇa.

sentences.zh: 涅槃亦曰泥洹，譯言滅度，亦言常樂我淨。

translations.literal: Nirvāṇa is also called nirvāṇa (níhuán); rendered "extinction and crossing over"; also called permanence, bliss, self, and purity.
translations.idiomatic: Nirvāṇa is also called nirvāṇa (níhuán), rendered "extinction and crossing over," and also described as permanence, bliss, self, and purity.

sentences.zh: 初釋迦說法，以人之性識根業各差，故有大乘小乘之說。

translations.literal: When Śākyamuni first taught the Law, because people's natures, faculties, and karmic roots differed, there were teachings of Mahayana and Hinayana.
translations.idiomatic: When Śākyamuni first taught the Law, because people's natures, faculties, and karmic roots differed, he expounded both Mahayana and Hinayana teachings.

sentences.zh: 至是謝世，弟子大迦葉與阿難等五百人，追共撰述，綴以文字，集載為十二部。

translations.literal: When he then departed the world, the disciples Mahākāśyapa, Ānanda, and five hundred others together pursued and compiled his teachings, arranged them in written form, and collected them into twelve divisions.
translations.idiomatic: When he departed the world, Mahākāśyapa, Ānanda, and five hundred other disciples compiled his teachings, set them down in writing, and collected them into twelve divisions.

sentences.zh: 後數百年，有羅漢菩薩，相繼著論，贊明其義。

translations.literal: After several centuries, arhats and bodhisattvas in succession wrote treatises, praising and clarifying the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Centuries later, arhats and bodhisattvas in succession wrote treatises praising and clarifying the meaning.

sentences.zh: 然佛所說，我滅度後，正法五百年，像法一千年，末法三千年，其義如此。

translations.literal: Yet the Buddha said: "After my parinirvāṇa, the correct Dharma lasts five hundred years, the semblance Dharma one thousand years, the final Dharma three thousand years"—the meaning is thus.
translations.idiomatic: The Buddha said: "After my parinirvāṇa, the correct Dharma will last five hundred years, the semblance Dharma one thousand years, and the final Dharma three thousand years"—the meaning is thus.

sentences.zh: 推尋典籍，自漢已上，中國未傳。

translations.literal: Searching through the records, from Han and earlier, China had not yet received the transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Searching the records, one finds that before Han times China had not yet received the transmission.

sentences.zh: 或雲久以流布，遭秦之世，所以堙滅。

translations.literal: Some say it had long been disseminated, but in the age of Qin it was buried and extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Some say it had long been disseminated but was buried and extinguished during the Qin dynasty.

sentences.zh: 其後張騫使西域，蓋聞有浮屠之教。

translations.literal: Later Zhang Qian was envoy to the Western Regions, and vaguely heard of the teaching of Fútú.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Zhang Qian was envoy to the Western Regions, he vaguely heard of the teaching of Fútú.

sentences.zh: 哀帝時，博士弟子秦景使伊存口授浮屠經，中土聞之，未之信也。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Ai, the academy student Qin Jing had Yicun orally transmit the Buddhist scripture; the central lands heard of it but did not yet believe.
translations.idiomatic: In the reign of Emperor Ai, the academy student Qin Jing had Yicun orally transmit a Buddhist scripture; the central lands heard of it but did not yet believe.

sentences.zh: 後漢明帝夜夢金人飛行殿庭，以問於朝，而傅毅以佛對。

translations.literal: Later Han Emperor Ming dreamed at night of a golden man flying in the palace courtyard; he asked the court, and Fu Yi answered concerning the Buddha.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Later Han dreamed one night of a golden man flying in the palace courtyard; he asked the court, and Fu Yi answered that it was the Buddha.

sentences.zh: 帝遣郎中蔡愔及秦景使天竺求之，得佛經四十二章及釋迦立像。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched Palace Attendant Cai Yin and Qin Jing as envoys to India to seek it; they obtained the Sutra in Forty-two Sections and a standing image of Śākyamuni.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched Palace Attendant Cai Yin and Qin Jing as envoys to India to seek it; they obtained the Sutra in Forty-two Sections and a standing image of Śākyamuni.

sentences.zh: 並與沙門攝摩騰、竺法蘭東還。

translations.literal: Together with the monks Kāśyapa Mātanga and Zhu Falan they returned east.
translations.idiomatic: Together with the monks Kāśyapa Mātanga and Zhu Falan they returned east.

sentences.zh: 愔之來也，以白馬負經，因立白馬寺於洛城雍門西以處之。

translations.literal: When Yin arrived, a white horse carried the scriptures; therefore White Horse Monastery was established west of Yong Gate in Luoyang to house them.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin arrived, a white horse carried the scriptures; White Horse Monastery was therefore established west of Yong Gate in Luoyang to house them.

sentences.zh: 其經緘于蘭台石室，而又畫像於清涼台及顯節陵上。

translations.literal: The scriptures were sealed in the Stone Chamber of the Orchid Terrace, and images were also painted on the Cool Terrace and atop the Xianjie Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: The scriptures were sealed in the Stone Chamber of the Orchid Terrace, and images were also painted on the Cool Terrace and atop the Xianjie Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 章帝時，楚王英以崇敬佛法聞，西域沙門，齎佛經而至者甚眾。

translations.literal: In Emperor Zhang's time, Prince Liu Ying of Chu was known for revering the Buddhist Law; Buddhist monks from the Western Regions bearing scriptures who arrived were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Zhang's time, Prince Liu Ying of Chu was known for revering the Buddhist Law, and many monks from the Western Regions arrived bearing Buddhist scriptures.

sentences.zh: 永平中，法蘭又譯《十住經》。

translations.literal: During the Yongping era, Falan again translated the Daśabhūmika Sūtra.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongping era, Falan again translated the Daśabhūmika Sūtra.

sentences.zh: 其餘傳譯，多未能通。

translations.literal: The rest of the transmitted translations mostly failed to achieve full comprehension.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the other transmitted translations failed to achieve full comprehension.

sentences.zh: 至桓帝時，有安息國沙門安靜，齎經至洛，翻譯最為通解。

translations.literal: By Emperor Huan's time there was the Parthian monk An Qing, who brought scriptures to Luoyang; his translations were most lucid and comprehensible.
translations.idiomatic: By Emperor Huan's time the Parthian monk An Qing had brought scriptures to Luoyang; his translations were the most lucid and comprehensible.

sentences.zh: 靈帝時，有月支沙門支讖、天竺沙門竺佛朔等，並翻佛經。

translations.literal: In Emperor Ling's time there were the Yuezhi monk Lokakṣema and the Indian monk Zhu Foshuo, among others, who all translated Buddhist scriptures.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Ling's time the Yuezhi monk Lokakṣema, the Indian monk Zhu Foshuo, and others all translated Buddhist scriptures.

sentences.zh: 而支讖所譯《泥洹經》二卷，學者以為大得本旨。

translations.literal: Lokakṣema's translation of the Nirvana Sutra in two scrolls—scholars held that it greatly captured the essential meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Lokakṣema's two-scroll translation of the Nirvana Sutra was held by scholars to capture the essential meaning admirably.

sentences.zh: 漢末，太守竺融，亦崇佛法。

translations.literal: At the end of Han, Prefect Zhu Rong also revered the Buddhist Law.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Han, Prefect Zhu Rong also revered the Buddhist Law.

sentences.zh: 三國時，有西域沙門康僧會，齎佛經至吳譯之，吳主孫權，甚大敬信。

translations.literal: In the Three Kingdoms period there was the Western Regions monk Kang Senghui, who brought Buddhist scriptures to Wu and translated them; Wu's ruler Sun Quan greatly honored and believed in him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Three Kingdoms period the Western Regions monk Kang Senghui brought Buddhist scriptures to Wu and translated them; Wu's ruler Sun Quan greatly honored and believed in him.

sentences.zh: 魏黃初中，中國人始依佛戒，剃髮為僧。

translations.literal: In the Huangchu era of Wei, Chinese for the first time took the Buddhist precepts, shaved their heads, and became monks.
translations.idiomatic: In the Huangchu era of Wei, Chinese for the first time took the Buddhist precepts, shaved their heads, and became monks.

sentences.zh: 先是西域沙門來此，譯《小品經》，首尾乖舛，未能通解。

translations.literal: Before this, Western Regions monks had come here and translated the Lesser Perfection of Wisdom Sutra; beginning and end were inconsistent, and full comprehension was not achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Western Regions monks had come and translated the Lesser Perfection of Wisdom Sutra, but the text was inconsistent from beginning to end and full comprehension was not achieved.

sentences.zh: 甘露中，有硃仕行者，往西域，至於闐國，得經九十章，晉元康中，至鄴譯之，題曰《放光般若經》。

translations.literal: During Ganlu, there was the lay practitioner Zhu Shixing, who went to the Western Regions, reached Khotan, and obtained ninety fascicles of scripture; in the Yuanzhang era of Jin he reached Ye and translated them, titled the Larger Prajñāpāramitā Sutra.
translations.idiomatic: During the Ganlu era the lay practitioner Zhu Shixing went to the Western Regions, reached Khotan, and obtained ninety fascicles of scripture; in the Yuanzhang era of Jin he reached Ye and translated them under the title Larger Prajñāpāramitā Sutra.

sentences.zh: 太始中，有月支沙門竺法護，西游諸國，大得佛經，至洛翻譯，部數甚多。

translations.literal: During Taishi, there was the Yuezhi monk Dharmarakṣa, who traveled west through various kingdoms, obtained many Buddhist scriptures in great number, came to Luoyang and translated—the titles were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taishi era the Yuezhi monk Dharmarakṣa traveled west through various kingdoms, obtained a great many Buddhist scriptures, came to Luoyang, and translated a very large number of titles.

sentences.zh: 佛教東流，自此而盛。

translations.literal: Buddhism flowing eastward from this point flourished greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhism's eastward transmission flourished greatly from this point onward.

sentences.zh: 石勒時，常山沙門衛道安，性聰敏，誦經日至萬餘言。

translations.literal: In Shi Le's time there was the Changshan monk Shi Dao'an, intelligent by nature, reciting scriptures daily to the amount of ten thousand-plus words.
translations.idiomatic: In Shi Le's time the Changshan monk Shi Dao'an was intelligent by nature and recited more than ten thousand words of scripture daily.

sentences.zh: 以胡僧所譯《維摩》《法華》，未盡深旨，精思十年，心了神悟，乃正其乖舛，宣揚解釋。

translations.literal: Because the Vimalakīrti and Lotus Sūtras as translated by Central Asian monks had not fully conveyed their deepest meaning, he pondered deeply for ten years until his mind was clear and his spirit enlightened; then he corrected their inconsistencies and proclaimed interpretations.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Vimalakīrti and Lotus Sūtras as translated by Central Asian monks had not fully conveyed their deepest meaning, he pondered deeply for ten years until his mind was clear and his spirit enlightened; then he corrected their inconsistencies and expounded their meaning.

sentences.zh: 時中國紛擾，四方隔絕，道安乃率門徒，南游新野，欲令玄宗所在流布，分遣弟子，各趨諸方。

translations.literal: At the time China was in turmoil and the four directions were cut off; Dao'an then led his disciples south to Xinye, wishing the profound teaching to be disseminated everywhere, and dispatched disciples each hurrying to various regions.
translations.idiomatic: At the time China was in turmoil and the four directions were cut off; Dao'an led his disciples south to Xinye, wishing the profound teaching to spread everywhere, and dispatched disciples to various regions.

sentences.zh: 法性詣揚州，法和入蜀，道安與慧遠之襄陽。

translations.literal: Fahsing went to Yangzhou, Fahe entered Shu, and Dao'an with Huiyuan went to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fahsing went to Yangzhou, Fahe entered Shu, and Dao'an with Huiyuan went to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 後至長安，苻堅甚敬之。

translations.literal: Later he reached Chang'an; Fu Jian greatly honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Later he reached Chang'an, where Fu Jian greatly honored him.

sentences.zh: 道安素聞天竺沙門鳩摩羅什，思通法門，勸堅致之。

translations.literal: Dao'an had long heard of the Indian monk Kumārajīva, wished to penetrate the gates of the Dharma, and urged Fu Jian to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Dao'an had long heard of the Indian monk Kumārajīva, wished to penetrate the gates of the Dharma, and urged Fu Jian to summon him.

sentences.zh: 什亦聞安令問，遙拜致敬。

translations.literal: Kumārajīva also heard of Dao'an's fine reputation and bowed in homage from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Kumārajīva also heard of Dao'an's fine reputation and bowed in homage from afar.

sentences.zh: 姚萇弘始二年，羅什至長安，時道安卒後已二十載矣，什深慨恨。

translations.literal: In the second year of Hongshi under Yao Chang, Kumārajīva reached Chang'an; by then Dao'an had died twenty years earlier, and Kumārajīva deeply lamented this.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Hongshi under Yao Chang, Kumārajīva reached Chang'an; Dao'an had already died twenty years earlier, and Kumārajīva deeply lamented this.

sentences.zh: 什之來也，大譯經論，道安所正，與什所譯，義如一，初無乖舛。

translations.literal: When Kumārajīva came, he translated many scriptures and treatises; what Dao'an had corrected and what Kumārajīva translated agreed in meaning, with never an inconsistency at the start.
translations.idiomatic: When Kumārajīva came, he translated many scriptures and treatises; what Dao'an had corrected and what Kumārajīva translated agreed in meaning from the outset, without inconsistency.

sentences.zh: 初，晉元熙中，新豐沙門智猛，策杖西行，到華氏城，得《泥洹經》及《僧祗律》，東至高昌，譯《泥洹》為二十卷。

translations.literal: At the beginning, in the Yuanxi era of Jin, the Xinfeng monk Zhimeng, staff in hand traveled west, reached Huvishka's city, obtained the Nirvana Sutra and the Saṃghikavīnaya, went east to Gaochang, and translated the Nirvana Sutra into twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanxi era of Jin the Xinfeng monk Zhimeng traveled west with staff in hand, reached Huvishka's city, obtained the Nirvana Sutra and the Saṃghikavīnaya, went east to Gaochang, and translated the Nirvana Sutra into twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 後有天竺沙門曇摩羅讖複齎胡本，來至河西。

translations.literal: Later the Indian monk Dharmarakṣa again brought a Central Asian original and came to the Hexi region.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Indian monk Dharmarakṣa again brought a Central Asian original and came to the Hexi region.

sentences.zh: 沮渠蒙遜遣使至高昌取猛本，欲相參驗，未還而蒙遜破滅。

translations.literal: Juqu Mengxun sent an envoy to Gaochang to fetch Zhimeng's text, intending to compare and verify them; before he returned, Mengxun was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun sent an envoy to Gaochang to fetch Zhimeng's text for comparison and verification, but before the envoy returned, Mengxun was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 姚萇弘始十年，猛本始至長安，譯為三十卷。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Hongshi under Yao Chang, Zhimeng's text finally reached Chang'an and was translated into thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Hongshi under Yao Chang, Zhimeng's text finally reached Chang'an and was translated into thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 曇摩羅讖又譯《金光明》等經。

translations.literal: Dharmarakṣa also translated the Suvarṇaprabhāsa and other sūtras.
translations.idiomatic: Dharmarakṣa also translated the Suvarṇaprabhāsa and other sūtras.

sentences.zh: 時胡僧至長安者數十輩，惟鳩摩羅什才德最優。

translations.literal: At the time several tens of Central Asian monks reached Chang'an; only Kumārajīva's talent and virtue were supreme.
translations.idiomatic: At the time several tens of Central Asian monks reached Chang'an, but Kumārajīva's talent and virtue were supreme.

sentences.zh: 其所譯則《維摩》、《法華》、《成實論》等諸經，及曇無懺所譯《金光明》，曇摩羅懺譯《泥洹》等經，並為大乘之學。

translations.literal: What he translated—the Vimalakīrti, Lotus, Satyasiddhi Śāstra and other scriptures, together with the Suvarṇaprabhāsa translated by Dharmagupta and the Nirvana Sutra translated by Dharmakṣema—all belong to Mahayana learning.
translations.idiomatic: What he translated—the Vimalakīrti, Lotus, and Satyasiddhi Śāstra among other scriptures, together with the Suvarṇaprabhāsa translated by Dharmagupta and the Nirvana Sutra translated by Dharmakṣema—all belong to Mahayana learning.

sentences.zh: 而什又譯《十誦律》，天竺沙門佛陀耶舍譯《長阿含經》及《四方律》，兜佉勒沙門曇摩難提譯《增一阿含經》，曇摩耶舍譯《阿毗曇論》，並為小乘之學。

translations.literal: Kumārajīva also translated the Daśadhammaka Vinaya; the Indian monk Buddhayaśas translated the Dīrghāgama and the Four-part Vinaya; the Tokharian monk Dharmanandi translated the Ekottarāgama; Dharmayaśas translated the Abhidharma treatise—all belong to Hinayana learning.
translations.idiomatic: Kumārajīva also translated the Daśadhammaka Vinaya; the Indian monk Buddhayaśas translated the Dīrghāgama and the Four-part Vinaya; the Tokharian monk Dharmanandi translated the Ekottarāgama; and Dharmayaśas translated the Abhidharma treatise—all belong to Hinayana learning.

sentences.zh: 其餘經論，不可勝記。

translations.literal: The remaining scriptures and treatises are beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining scriptures and treatises are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 自是佛法流通，極于四海矣。

translations.literal: From this the Buddhist Law spread everywhere, reaching to the furthest seas.
translations.idiomatic: From this point the Buddhist Law spread everywhere, reaching to the furthest seas.

sentences.zh: 東晉隆安中，又有罽賓沙門僧伽提婆譯《增一阿含經》及《中阿含經》。

translations.literal: In the Long'an era of Eastern Jin, the Gandhāran monk Saṇghadeva again translated the Ekottarāgama and Madhyamāgama.
translations.idiomatic: In the Long'an era of Eastern Jin the Gandhāran monk Saṇghadeva again translated the Ekottarāgama and Madhyamāgama.

sentences.zh: 義熙中，沙門支法領從于闐國得《華嚴經》三萬六千偈，至金陵宣譯。

translations.literal: In the Yixi era, the monk Zhi Faling obtained from Khotan the Avataṃsaka Sūtra of thirty-six thousand gāthās and reached Jinling to preach and translate it.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yixi era the monk Zhi Faling obtained from Khotan the Avataṃsaka Sūtra of thirty-six thousand gāthās and reached Jinling to preach and translate it.

sentences.zh: 又有沙門法顯，自長安遊天竺，經三十余國，隨有經律之處，學其書語，譯而寫之。

translations.literal: There was also the monk Faxian, who from Chang'an traveled to India, passed through more than thirty states, and wherever there were scriptures and vinaya, learned their scripts and languages, translated and wrote them down.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the monk Faxian, who traveled from Chang'an to India, passed through more than thirty states, and wherever scriptures and vinaya were found, learned the local scripts and languages, translated them, and wrote them down.

sentences.zh: 還至金陵，與天竺禪師跋羅參共辯定，謂《僧祗律》，學者傳之。

translations.literal: He returned to Jinling, and together with the Indian meditation master Buddharāta jointly collated and settled [the text], called the Saṃghikavīnaya; scholars transmitted it.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Jinling and, together with the Indian meditation master Buddharāta, collated and settled the Saṃghikavīnaya, which scholars thereafter transmitted.

sentences.zh: 齊梁及陳，並有外國沙門。

translations.literal: In Qi, Liang, and Chen, there were all foreign monks.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi, Liang, and Chen, foreign monks were present in each.

sentences.zh: 然所宣譯，無大名部可為法門者。
